thread:
alice.ops: Heads up — acme corp seeing spikes of SSL handshake failures to our private VPC endpoint when routed through their corp proxy. Errors: intermittent 502 / TLS handshake_failure. Appears to be cipher/version negotiation issue.

acme-corp-sre: Yep, we've got lots of failed upstreams in our gateway logs. curl shows 'SSL: tlsv1 alert protocol version' and the proxy logs a TLS handshake failure. Impacting our real-time inference calls (timeouts + retries).

matt.support: Thanks—can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and an openssl s_client output from a failing host? Also which proxy appliance/version are you running? @dena.netops FYI. :eyes:

acme-corp-sre: Repro steps: (from inside corp network)
```
curl -v --tlsv1.2 https://private.redwood.internal/v1/engines/text-gen/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```
Proxy: F5 BIG-IP LTM (13.1.0), SSL profile with strict corporate cipher policy (server-side cipher order enforced).

alice.ops: Here's the openssl run from our side (failing path):
```
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.internal:443 -servername private.redwood.internal -tls1_2 -cipher ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
CONNECTED(00000003)
139845...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1544:SSL alert number 70
---
no peer certificate available
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
SSL handshake has read 7 bytes and written 312 bytes
```
Ticket: looks like the proxy aborts before any certificate exchange.

dena.netops: F5s often enforce a server-preferred cipher order and drop client ECDHE offers if the server list doesn't include a matching RSA/ECDHE combo. Can you dump the cipher list your server presents? Also, do you use `ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on;` in nginx?

alice.ops: Nginx config snippet (serving the private endpoint):
```
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
ssl_ciphers "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:...:RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256";
ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on; # default in our image
```

matt.support: Two hypotheses: (1) proxy only allows RSA key exchange ciphers and drops pure ECDHE if server prefers ECDHE-ECDSA, (2) proxy is configured to disallow specific EC curves or TLS1.2 extensions (SNI/ALPN mismatch). Both can manifest as handshake_failure with little detail.

kevin.platform: Can we reproduce by forcing the client to use RSA-only ciphers to see if it succeeds? Try: `openssl s_client -connect ... -cipher "RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256" -tls1_2`. Also paste `openssl s_client -connect <proxy-ip>:443 -servername private.redwood.internal -tls1_2 -alpn http/1.1` to confirm ALPN behavior.

acme-corp-sre: Ran RSA test, it succeeds:
```
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.internal:443 -servername private.redwood.internal -tls1_2 -cipher "RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256"
CONNECTED(00000003)
...verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN = private.redwood.internal
---
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.2
    Cipher    : RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
```
So when we force RSA it works. Default ECDHE attempt fails.

dena.netops: That confirms the proxy is dropping ECDHE offers or the server prefers a certificate/key type that the proxy doesn't like. Quick checklist:
- Does the server present an ECDSA cert? (ECDSA certs + server-pref cipher order can cause mismatches with some proxies)
- Does the proxy policy explicitly exclude ECDHE curves (e.g., P-256)?
- Is SNI being rewritten/stripped by the proxy? (that would make cert mismatch)

alice.ops: Server cert is RSA (not ECDSA). We do prefer ECDHE ciphers first in the list and `ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on` is set. So the server prefers ECDHE-RSA when available.

matt.support: If forcing RSA ciphers fixes it, short-term mitigation options:
- Reorder server ciphers to prefer RSA-based TLS_RSA/ECDHE-RSA combos earlier (or disable server-prefer so client chooses compatible cipher).
- Ask customer to relax proxy cipher policy to allow ECDHE with our ciphers/curves.
- Route that customer's traffic to hosted breakout temporarily (no corp proxy).

alice.ops: Trying a config tweak now — turning `ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off` and moving RSA fallback earlier in `ssl_ciphers`. Will roll a canary for one host.

deploy-bot: rolling deploy canary -> private-vpc-service/sha:aa1b2c3 -> host-7

acme-corp-sre: Can you also confirm SNI is intact? Our proxy used to strip SNI for some backend hosts. If SNI gets stripped the F5 will select the wrong SSL profile.

alice.ops: Verified with tcpdump: SNI present in ClientHello.

matt.support: Nice. Keep an eye on latency after the canary; forcing RSA might increase CPU but will restore connectivity. Also note TLS1.3 clients will still prefer ECDHE; most TLS1.3 ciphers are ECDHE-only. If the customer's proxy doesn't support TLS1.3 properly we might see fallback.

acme-corp-sre: After canary change we see successful connections from our proxy. 502s drop to baseline. :tada:

dena.netops: For long term: recommend adding TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 with compatible curves to the server, but keep an RSA fallback at a lower priority. Also coordinate with acme's security team to allow ECDHE curves in their F5 SSL profile.

kevin.platform: Filed ENG-PLAT task to adjust default private deployment cipher order and add a compatibility matrix doc for enterprise proxies. Ticket: PLAT-7642.

matt.support: Marking resolved for now — customer connectivity restored with canary. Follow-ups: document recommended nginx settings and an ops playbook for proxy-related TLS troubleshooting.

alice.ops: Thanks team. Will post the playbook + remediation steps in #support after we finish write-up. :memo:
